cards.content:
**Location:** The chip at the top of each page shows the location you are looking at. Tap it to switch. Every page then shows only that location.

**Names:** A word that every device in a location starts with, such as "ACME", is left off, so "ACME Hallway NE" shows as "Hallway NE" everywhere.

**Overview:** Usage now, energy today and this month, alerts, and what uses the most.

**Groups:** The energy of each group. **3D** shows the groups as rooms, with the lights that are on.

**Controls:** Switch lights, sockets, relays and AC, and see the power they draw.

**Devices:** **Map** shows how the devices connect. **List** shows every device with its type and readings. Tap a device for its power and energy; the rest is under Technical details.

**Reports:** Charts and figures for any period, opening on today. Export them as a PDF.

**Alerts:** What needs attention now, what happened in the last 7 days, and your alert rules.

**Setup:** For administrators: the main device, the wiring, automations and alert rules. Tenant admins manage groups under Setup, Locations, and rename or move a device from its own page under Devices. Locations and new devices are added by your administrator.

**Usage now:** How much is being used at this moment, from its main device.

**Usage today, Usage this month:** Energy used since midnight, or since the 1st. "Since" shows when recording started later than that.

**Cost:** Energy multiplied by the location's price per kWh, set under Setup, Locations. With the exchange price, each hour is costed at that hour's own price. Every cost says whether VAT is included. It is an estimate, not your invoice.

**Price now:** What one kWh costs at this moment, and how that compares with today's average.

**Price per kWh, every 15 minutes:** The price from now to the last one published, usually up to tomorrow night. Hover or tap a bar for its time and price. It is not your invoice. Every cost in the portal is an estimate.

**Highest demand:** The hour this month with the highest average power, and when it was.

**Alerts:** A red bell with a number when something needs attention, a green bell when all is well. Tap it to open Alerts.

**What uses the most today:** The meters that make up the total, by today's energy.

**Energy by hour, by day:** Total, or split by device. The dots are yesterday, for comparison.

**Lights:** Tap a light to switch it. It shows Turning on… until the device confirms, then On or Off with the power it draws now, so you can see it worked. No response means the device did not answer. Each group has On and Off for all its lights, with its power. **All off** at the top asks before it switches the whole location. After a group is switched, **Undo** shows for a few seconds.

**Sockets and relays:** Their own tab, switched one at a time. All off and the group buttons never touch them.

**Climate:** Air conditioning.

**Automations:** Administrators make them under Setup, Automations: they switch devices at a set time on chosen days. Give each one a name, then choose a group, or any devices of the location. For a group, tick which of its devices it switches: lights are ticked, sockets and relays are not. The switch beside an automation turns it on or off, and each one shows when it last ran. Alerts, Automations lists every time one ran.

Every device has one type, which says what it is for.

**Energy meter:** Only measures. A device without a relay is always a meter.

**Light:** A relay that switches lights. Lights are what All off and the group buttons switch.

**Socket:** A relay that powers a socket.

**Relay:** A relay for an appliance, such as a boiler, fridge or water machine.

**AC:** Air conditioning.

Measuring is not a type: every device that measures counts in the energy figures, whatever its type. A switch is treated as a relay unless Home Assistant exposes a light entity for it or it has a Light label. Add a Socket, Relay, AC or Energy meter label to set the other types.

**Now:** What needs attention at this moment.

**Last 7 days:** What happened this week, with each time it happened.

**Automations:** Each time an automation ran in the last 7 days, and which devices it switched. "Nothing needed switching" means every device was already as it should be.

**Your own rules:** Administrators make them under Setup, Alerts: choose a device, what to watch, above or below a limit, and Warning or Critical. Each rule is a Threshold helper in Home Assistant, which checks it all the time, even when nobody has the app open. A short spike counts too.

**Device limits:** Some meters have their own limits, such as high voltage. Your administrator changes them in Home Assistant.

**Phone notifications:** An automation in Home Assistant that sends a message when a rule turns on.

**Critical (red):** Needs dealing with now. **Warning (amber):** Worth watching.

**Not sending readings:** A device sent no readings: it is offline, has no power, or has lost its network. Last 7 days lists times of an hour or longer.

**Connection drops:** The connection to the devices dropped briefly. Live readings pause for a few seconds; totals are not affected.

**Power (W, kW):** How much is being used right now. 1,000 W = 1 kW.

**Energy (kWh):** Power used over time, and what you are billed for. 1 kW for 1 hour = 1 kWh.

**Voltage (V):** The strength of the supply. Normal is 207 to 253 V.

**Frequency (Hz):** How fast the mains alternates. It should stay close to 50 Hz.

**Power factor:** How much of the supplied power does useful work. Closer to 1 (100%) is better.

**Phases A, B, C:** The three supply lines of a three-phase connection.

**Constant use (W):** Power still used when the building is quiet, estimated from weekends or the quietest hours.

**Readings received (%):** How much of the period has readings. Gaps are never filled in.

**Unmeasured:** Energy a device used that the devices under it did not measure. Kitchen 20 kWh with grills 8 kWh leaves 12 kWh unmeasured.

**Partial:** A device has no reading, so the figure is incomplete and is not guessed.

**Check wiring:** The devices under a device add up to more than it does.

**Main device:** The device whose figures Overview shows, usually the one at the incoming supply. Chosen under Setup.

**Devices under it:** The devices a device feeds. In Setup, Wiring, open a device and tick the devices under it. A device under a real meter is not added on top of it: that meter already measured it.

**Virtual device:** Not a physical device. It adds up the devices you tick under it. It is also in Home Assistant as two Sum helpers, energy and power, to use in automations, cards and alert rules.

**Not counted twice:** A device under another device is shown on its own, but not added to totals, because the device above already includes it.

**Locations and groups:** A location is one site of the tenant; your administrator adds locations. Groups organise a location's devices and can sit inside other groups. Tenant admins add, rename and delete groups under Setup, Locations. A group adds up the devices in it and in the groups inside it.

**Adding a device:** Your administrator assigns a new device to a location under Administration, Devices. To put it in a group, open it under Devices and choose the group.

**Removing a device:** Your administrator removes it from the tenant under Administration, Devices. A device that a virtual device, an automation or an alert rule still uses has to be taken out of those first.

**Price per kWh:** Choose a source for each location. You can switch anytime without losing the other choices.

**Bill:** upload the tenant's bill as a PDF or photos. The price is the whole bill with VAT divided by its kWh, including all listed charges. It stays at that saved price until another bill is used.

**IBEX:** uses the live exchange price plus an optional margin and fees before VAT, then adds VAT. The price changes every 15 minutes.

**Fixed:** enter one custom price per kWh, VAT included.

Until a source is selected, Home Assistant's price helper is used and its VAT is shown as not stated. If the IBEX price stops coming in, the helper stands in and Setup says so. The AI model and its instructions are in bill-reader.json, in Home Assistant's www folder.
